clinicalPearls: Autosomal dominant predisposition to medullary thyroid carcinoma caused by activating germline variants in the RET proto-oncogene
It is now regarded as a variant of MEN2A in which medullary thyroid carcinoma occurs without phaeochromocytoma or hyperparathyroidism
Medullary carcinoma arises from calcitonin-producing parafollicular C cells, so calcitonin is the key tumour marker
The specific RET codon variant guides risk stratification and the recommended timing of prophylactic thyroidectomy
Genetic testing of at-risk relatives allows pre-symptomatic identification and genotype-directed surgery before cancer develops
Management centres on total thyroidectomy, either therapeutic or prophylactic, with biochemical follow-up using calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen
Because phaeochromocytoma can coexist in the broader MEN2 spectrum, exclude catecholamine excess before any surgery in RET carriers
reference.pathophysiology: RET encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase essential for the development and function of neural-crest-derived tissues, including thyroid C cells. Activating germline variants cause constitutive, ligand-independent kinase signalling that drives proliferation of parafollicular C cells, progressing from C-cell hyperplasia to medullary thyroid carcinoma. Because the tumour originates from calcitonin-secreting cells, circulating calcitonin rises and serves as a sensitive marker of tumour burden. The particular codon affected determines how strongly the kinase is activated and therefore the aggressiveness and age of onset of the carcinoma, which is why genotype directs the timing of prophylactic thyroidectomy. In the familial form the oncogenic RET signalling is largely confined to the thyroid C cells, without the adrenal or parathyroid involvement seen in other MEN2 subtypes.
additionalInvestigations: Serum calcitonin as the principal tumour marker, including stimulated testing where appropriate
Carcinoembryonic antigen for monitoring tumour burden
Neck ultrasound for thyroid nodules and cervical lymphadenopathy
Biochemical exclusion of phaeochromocytoma (plasma or urinary metanephrines) before surgery
Serum calcium and parathyroid hormone to assess for parathyroid involvement in the wider MEN2 spectrum
RET gene sequencing with codon-specific risk classification
redFlags: Rapidly rising calcitonin or carcinoembryonic antigen indicating progressive or recurrent disease
Cervical lymphadenopathy or a fixed thyroid mass suggesting advanced carcinoma
Unrecognised phaeochromocytoma precipitating a crisis during thyroid surgery
reference.prognosis: When prophylactic thyroidectomy is performed early, guided by genotype and before metastatic spread, the outlook is excellent and cure is achievable; prognosis worsens with delayed diagnosis, nodal or distant metastases, and persistently elevated calcitonin.
pitfalls: Proceeding to thyroid surgery without first excluding a phaeochromocytoma
Delaying prophylactic thyroidectomy beyond the genotype-recommended age
Assuming the familial form never involves the adrenal or parathyroid across the MEN2 spectrum
Failing to test and counsel at-risk relatives for the dominant RET variant
references: OMIM entry for familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
management: Perform total thyroidectomy, with prophylactic timing guided by the RET codon risk category or therapeutic surgery with lymph-node dissection when carcinoma is established
Exclude and treat any phaeochromocytoma by measuring metanephrines before surgery to avoid an intraoperative hypertensive crisis
Provide lifelong levothyroxine replacement after thyroidectomy
Use a selective RET kinase inhibitor (selpercatinib or pralsetinib) for advanced, progressive or metastatic medullary carcinoma
Maintain biochemical surveillance with calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen to detect residual or recurrent disease
Undertake RET genetic testing with cascade screening of relatives to enable pre-symptomatic, genotype-directed prophylactic thyroidectomy
Coordinate multidisciplinary endocrinology, endocrine surgery and clinical genetics follow-up
